Pedagogy

Learning by understanding and by doing

Connecting fundamental knowledge with concrete situations: case studies, projects, presentations, immersions and hands-on professional scenarios, with a reference orientation of 40 % theory and 60 % practice.

Our educational approach

A reference orientation of 40 % theoretical input and 60 % practice, projects, tutorials, field work, internships and immersions, subject to the approved curriculum of each programme.

Learning by understanding and by doing

ABS's teaching aims to connect fundamental knowledge with concrete situations. Depending on the programme and the resources available, learning may draw on case studies, exercises, tutorials, projects, presentations, visits and professional immersions. The goal is to advance the student in analysis, method, communication and the ability to produce a well-argued piece of work.

Projects as a common thread

Projects enable students to mobilise several skills around a problem or a deliverable: a study, a file, a prototype, an action plan, a presentation or a report. Objectives, assessment criteria and deadlines are explained at the start of each module.

Languages and international openness

English is conceived as a transversal skill to be developed progressively throughout the programmes. It combines comprehension, expression, professional vocabulary and hands-on scenarios. For International Relations and Affairs, Spanish is considered as a complementary language, subject to validation of the teaching hours and arrangements. Any announcement of TOEIC, IELTS or other certification is limited to the schemes actually available and authorised.

Digital skills and artificial intelligence

Digital skills are playing a growing role in the professions. ABS promotes the reasoned use of digital tools and a gradual introduction to artificial intelligence, taking into account students' level, the needs of each field, data protection, critical thinking and academic integrity.

Personal development and professional readiness

Training also includes dimensions essential to professional life: public speaking, time management, teamwork, organisation, interpersonal skills, leading meetings, stress management and preparation for employment. The exact activities depend on the academic calendar and are announced once confirmed.

Internships and immersions

Internships, visits and immersions are opportunities to better understand the professions and working environments. Their schedule, arrangements and mandatory or optional nature are specified in the official curriculum of each programme.

Bilingualism

French-English bilingualism, a strategic pillar of training

At ABS — African Business School, mastering French and English is a fundamental strand of every student's academic and professional journey. In an African environment characterised by linguistic diversity and the intensification of international exchanges, ABS aims to graduate professionals able to communicate, to negotiate, to present their ideas and to exercise their responsibilities in both languages.

Learning English is not limited to the class hours devoted to it: it is conceived as a skill progressively mobilised in courses, projects, research work, oral presentations, immersion activities and assessments.

Language content is tailored to the specialities — scientific and technical English in engineering, business English in administration, diplomatic English in international relations, media English in journalism and communication, and English applied to digital technologies in computer engineering.

A structured progression, from the Licence (Bachelor's degree) to the Master

This progression enables every student to develop measurable language skills and to prepare, according to their level and pathway, for international certifications such as TOEIC or IELTS.

Defences in French and in English

Viva voce defences are a major instrument of professional readiness and of assessing communication skills. At ABS, they are designed as opportunities to structure an argument, to present results, to answer a jury's questions and to defend one's proposals before an audience. Assessment arrangements may include:

  • Defences in French for academic projects and work;
  • Presentations or defences in English, depending on language level and pathway;
  • Bilingual defences, with a presentation in one language and a question-and-answer sequence in the other;
  • Executive summaries, abstracts or presentation materials in English;
  • Simulations of meetings, negotiations, conferences and job interviews in French and English.

The precise arrangements are defined in the curricula and assessment regulations. The progression is adapted to the level of study so that the language requirement serves as a learning objective rather than an unjustified obstacle to assessing disciplinary knowledge.

English tailored to each speciality

To bring bilingualism to life in practice, ABS encourages the progressive use of French and English in the teaching activities of all fields: documentary reading, bilingual presentations, international case studies, literature research, debates and professional simulations.

FieldEnglish
Engineering (geological, civil and mining)Scientific and technical English
Business administrationBusiness English
International relations and affairsDiplomatic English
Journalism and CommunicationMedia English
Computer engineeringEnglish applied to digital technologies

Immersions, projects and personal development

Immersions and field trips extend learning by confronting students with the realities of companies, institutions, laboratories, construction sites, media, international organisations and other professional environments. Where conditions allow, these activities include exercises in English: presenting an organisation, interviewing a professional, gathering information, giving an oral report or writing a bilingual summary.

ABS's educational model combines the mastery of knowledge with the development of personality, a sense of responsibility and initiative. Workshops on leadership, public speaking, negotiation, entrepreneurship, professional ethics, project management and citizenship are organised in French and, progressively, in English.

A coherent whole in the service of success

At ABS, French-English bilingualism, applied projects, defences, immersions, field trips and personal development form a coherent whole in the service of academic success and employability. Educating graduates who are competent in their speciality, able to work in French and in English, to defend their ideas with confidence and to carry a pan-African vision of development.
